question.problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-x}{{x}^{2}-1}, & x<1 \\ \frac{1}{x+1}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

I. $[-5,1)$

II. $[0,5]$

III. $[5,10]$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the extreme value theorem is only applicable to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

So, let's check whether the function is continuous on each of the intervals.

- The interval $[-5,1)$ is not closed, so the extreme value theorem is not applicable.

- Now, consider $[0,5].$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 1}(\frac{{x}^{2}-x}{{x}^{2}-1}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}(\frac{x(x-1)}{(x-1)(x+1)}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{x}{x+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}, \\ {lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 1}(\frac{1}{x+1})=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits from the left and from the right of $x=1$ are the same. Hence, $f(x)$ is continuous on the interval $[0,5],$ and the extreme value theorem is applicable on this interval.

- Finally, consider $[5,10].$ In this interval $f(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}$ and so $f(x)$ is continuous on $[5,10].$ Therefore, the extreme value theorem is applicable on this interval.

In conclusion, the correct answer is "II and III only".
